rad_text_en: Serial chest X-rays, performed after oral administration of radiopaque contrast agent:  Esophageal-pleural fistula located on the lateral aspect of the superior thoracic esophagus, with contrast extravasation. Right pneumothorax with stable appearance compared to previous examination. No other abnormalities compared to previous chest X-ray.  Re-evaluation at 18:42, after bronchial blocker insertion on the antero-basal right hemithorax:  Complete regression of the pneumothorax described above. Accentuation of interstitial peribroncho-vascular perihilar bilateral pattern. Basal pulmonary consolidation areas bilaterally. Right apico-axillary-lateral-basal pleural effusion. Contrast agent present para-esophagically in the superior thoracic region and at the level of the gastric foramen. Bronchial blocker projected laterally-basal on the right hemithorax. CVC, SNG, endotracheal tube with unchanged appearance compared to previous examinations. Gastrostomy present.
